sectionProgressions.description: Chromatic bass descent with open string resonance and country-blues slide bends
Smooth stepwise descent resolving on the dramatic major dominant G#7
Full ringing open chord stadium rock progression

harmonicFunction: C#m (vi) - Moody minor home of the intro and verse with country-jazz sophistication
E/B (I6/4) - Passing chord maintaining voice leading descent in the bass (C# → B → A → G#)
G#7 (V7/vi) - Secondary dominant with raised B# leading tone providing intense harmonic tension
E (I) - Triumphant resolution into the tonic major in the anthemic chorus

techniques.name: Chromatic Voice-Leading & Country Bending
techniques.description: Blending rich jazz-inflected chord voicings with country pedal-steel-inspired slides and bends on standard guitar

notes: Intro riff slides on the 4th, 3rd, and 2nd strings
Smooth stepwise bass descent: C# (5th fret A string) → B (2nd fret A) → A (open A) → G# (4th fret low E)
Open high B and E strings ringing as pedal drones
sequence: Fret the opening chromatic line starting on fret 4 of the A string
Slide into the C#m7 voicing and let the open strings ring
Execute the half-step bass descent to E/B and A
Barre the G#7 shape and accent beat 4
tips: Use a light touch with your fretting hand to avoid sharping the open strings
Dean DeLeo achieved his wide acoustic-electric stereo spread using a Gibson Les Paul and acoustic in unison
Emphasize the Major 3rd (B#) on the G#7 chord for maximum harmonic bite

techniques.name: Dean DeLeo's B-String Country Pedal Bends & Relative Major Modulation
techniques.description: Emulating Nashville pedal steel voice leading on a rock guitar by bending the B and G strings behind ringing open high strings, modulating from C# minor verses to E major choruses

notes: Country bend: 7th fret B string bent a whole step up to C# while holding the 7th fret high E string
Secondary dominant tension: G#7 (4-6-4-5-4-4) introducing the crucial B# leading tone
Tonic major lift: E (0-2-2-1-0-0) to Asus2 (X-0-2-2-0-0) with shimmering open B and E drones
sequence: Play the intro slide figure with gentle pick dynamics
Lead the bass down through C# → B → A → G#
Stab the G#7 chord firmly on beat 4 with crisp palm damping
Explode into full-strummed open E major on the chorus downbeat
tips: Use the middle position (both humbuckers) on a Les Paul to get DeLeo's hollow, bell-like intro tone
Hold the G#7 barre flat across the 4th fret so the high F# on string 1 rings out
Switch to the bridge pickup when hitting the heavy chorus strumming

sections.name: Intro Chromatic Slide Motif & Pedal Drones
sections.description: One of the most recognizable guitar intros in 90s rock, blending country slides and jazz chords.
notes: Slide smoothly into the C#m7 chord
Keep the descending bassline prominent
Let open strings ring over the chord shapes

sections.name: Verse 1 Descending Bass Voice-Leading
sections.description: The descending bass progression supporting Scott Weiland's soulful verse melody.
notes: Clean pick articulation on the lower strings
Full sustain on the G#7 dominant chord
Maintain relaxed 86 BPM pocket

sections.name: Chorus 1 Triumphant E Major Lift
sections.description: Massive open chord explosion into E major, Asus2, and C#m under 'Waiting on a Sunday afternoon'.
notes: Broad open strumming with ring on high E and B strings
Emphasize the punchy transition to Asus2
Lock in with the drum kick and snare

sections.name: Verse 2 Rhythmic Chug & Passing Tones
sections.description: Verse 2 adds subtle rhythmic palm-muting and vocal responses on the G#7 turnaround.
notes: Accentuate the bass walkdown notes on beats 1 and 3
Crisp choke on beat 4 before the G#7 chord
Warm overdriven tube tone

sections.name: Mid-Song Instrumental Break & Slide Lead
sections.description: DeLeo revisits the opening slide theme with singing sustain and melodic counterpoint.
notes: Smooth glissando slides between frets 4, 6, and 7
Sweet vibrato at the crest of the slide
Resolve cleanly into the final chorus blast

sections.name: Chorus 2 & Outro Ringing Cadence
sections.description: Final double chorus soaring into the fading acoustic-electric chord cadence.
notes: Wide open acoustic-electric strumming
Allow the top strings to ring sympathetically
Resolve on a ringing E major chord to end

guitar.pickup: Bridge humbucker for dirty crunch; middle position for intro

beginner.title: Chorus Open Chords
steps: Learn the E, Asus2, C#m, and A chord shapes
Strum in steady eighth notes at 86 BPM
Practice the dynamic shift from verse to chorus

intermediate.title: Intro Slide & Verse Progression
steps: Learn the intro chromatic sliding figure cleanly
Master the four-chord verse progression with descending bass (C#m → E/B → A → G#7)
Nail the timing of the G#7 dominant transition

advanced.title: Full Nuance & Studio Articulation
steps: Incorporate Dean DeLeo's subtle thumb-over bass notes and open string voicings
Perform the complete song with authentic studio tone and touch

commonMistakes: Muting the high open strings during the C#m7 and E/B voicings
Playing G# minor instead of G#7 (the major third B# is essential)
Rushing the relaxed, swaying 86 BPM tempo
practiceRoutine: 5 minutes: Intro slide lick isolated at 70 BPM → 86 BPM
5 minutes: Stepwise verse chord transitions with focus on bass movement
5 minutes: Chorus open chord dynamic strumming
5 minutes: Full playthrough with studio recording
focusAreas: Fretting accuracy on the G#7 barre shape
metronomeWork: Practice the intro slide at 70 BPM to ensure clean pitch placement
Build to album tempo of 86 BPM with accents on 2 and 4
